report.title: Google ships Gemini 3.5 Flash GA at I/O, replaces 3.x as default
report.summary: Gemini 3.5 Flash is now generally available via the Gemini API, AI Studio, Android Studio, and Google Antigravity — outperforming Gemini 3.1 Pro on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (76.2%) and MCP Atlas (83.6%) at less than half the cost of comparable frontier models. Drop-in for any app currently on 3.1 Flash; Gemini 3.5 Pro follows next month.

report.title: Google launches Gemini Omni Flash: any-input-to-video model now live
report.summary: Gemini Omni Flash — Google's new model that generates video from text, audio, image, and video inputs — is available today in Google Flow and on YouTube Shorts, with API access rolling out to developers in coming weeks. Consumer-facing first; enterprise API builders will need to wait for the broader rollout.

report.title: Google launches Managed Agents API on Antigravity platform
report.summary: A single API call to Google Antigravity now provisions a remote Linux sandbox where an agent can reason, plan, execute code, manage files, and browse the web — powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash and available via the Interactions API and AI Studio. Direct competitor to Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents for hosted agent infra.

report.title: Anthropic ships self-hosted sandboxes and MCP tunnels for Claude Managed Agents
report.summary: Self-hosted sandboxes (public beta) move tool execution onto customer infrastructure — via Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, or Vercel — while the agent loop stays on Anthropic's side; MCP tunnels (research preview, request access required) connect agents to private internal databases and APIs over an outbound-only encrypted channel with no inbound firewall changes. Both unblock enterprise deployments with data-residency or security-perimeter requirements.

report.title: Andrej Karpathy joins Anthropic for frontier LLM R&D
report.summary: Karpathy announced on May 19 that he has joined Anthropic to get back to frontier LLM research, citing the next few years as especially formative. No product change today, but a notable signal about where serious AI researchers are placing bets.

report.title: OpenAI previews public image verification tool with C2PA and SynthID
report.summary: OpenAI is previewing a public verification tool that checks whether an uploaded image was generated by ChatGPT, the OpenAI API, or Codex — combining C2PA Content Credentials with SynthID watermarks. Currently limited to OpenAI-generated content only; cross-platform support is on the roadmap.

report.title: Anthropic expands Project Glasswing with Claude Security public beta for vetted teams
report.summary: Anthropic opened Claude Security — a Mythos-class capability for scanning codebases, triaging vulnerabilities, and generating fixes — to eligible security teams in public beta under Project Glasswing, while reiterating that a general Mythos release is contingent on safeguards no company has built yet. Builders outside vetted security orgs still cannot access it.

learn.name: Google Antigravity 2.0 + Antigravity CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: Google's agent-first dev platform: managed remote sandboxes via one API call, new CLI.

detail.whatItDoes:
Antigravity 2.0 is Google's agent-first development platform, now shipping a CLI (`antigravity`) and a Managed Agents API. A single API call provisions a full remote Linux sandbox where the Gemini 3.5 Flash-powered agent can reason, plan, execute code, manage files, and browse the web — all in an isolated environment. Orchestration, credential masking, and hardened Git policies are built in. You can also extend the agent with custom instructions in AGENTS.md and SKILL.md files.

The Antigravity SDK lets you self-host the agent harness on your own infrastructure if you need more control. A WebMCP origin trial (Chrome 149+) is also shipping, proposing an open web standard so browser-based agents can call structured JavaScript functions and HTML forms natively.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend and full-stack engineers building agentic workflows on Google Cloud or using Gemini API. Teams already using Android Studio will benefit from the stable Android CLI and open-sourced Android Skills. Any developer who wants a hosted alternative to running a local Claude Code or Cursor session will find Managed Agents a direct drop-in.
pros: Single API call provisions a full remote Linux sandbox — no infra setup
Gemini 3.5 Flash powers it: GA today, 4x faster than rival frontier models on output tokens/s
AGENTS.md / SKILL.md config means no orchestration code for standard workflows
WebMCP origin trial opens a path to browser-native agent tool execution
cons: Gemini 3.5 Pro (the bigger reasoning model) is still in testing; not GA yet
Self-hosting the Antigravity harness requires the Antigravity SDK and your own infra — not turnkey
Managed Agents API pricing not publicly listed; costs for long-horizon agentic runs are unclear
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
### Prerequisites
- Node 20+ or Python 3.11+
- A Google Cloud project with billing enabled
- Gemini API key from [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com)

### 1. Install the Antigravity CLI

```bash
npm install -g @google/antigravity-cli
# or via pip
pip install google-antigravity
```

### 2. Authenticate

```bash
antigravity auth login
# Opens a browser OAuth flow tied to your Google account
```

### 3. Spin up a managed agent session

```bash
antigravity run --model gemini-3.5-flash \
  --task "Clone https://github.com/my-org/my-repo and run the test suite"
# Returns a session ID; streams logs to stdout
```

### 4. Use the Managed Agents REST API directly

```python
import requests, os

API_KEY = os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"]

resp = requests.post(
    "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/agents:run",
    headers={"x-goog-api-key": API_KEY},
    json={
        "model": "gemini-3.5-flash",
        "task": "Summarise the open GitHub issues in owner/repo",
        "tools": ["code_execution", "browser"]
    }
)
print(resp.json())
```

### 5. Add custom skills

Create an `AGENTS.md` at your repo root:

```markdown
# My Agent

## Skills
- name: run-tests
  description: Run the full pytest suite and return a pass/fail summary
  command: pytest --tb=short -q
```

Then register it:

```bash
antigravity agents register --file AGENTS.md --name my-project-agent
```

**Gotcha:** The `SKILL.md` and `AGENTS.md` convention is new and separate from the existing `gemini.json` config used in older Antigravity 1.x projects. Don't mix them — the CLI will warn you but won't error out, and the skill won't load silently.

learn.name: Claude Managed Agents: Self-Hosted Sandboxes + MCP Tunnels
learn.oneLineDescription: Run Claude agent tool execution inside your own infra; connect private APIs via encrypted tunnel.

detail.whatItDoes: Claude Managed Agents now supports two new enterprise-facing deployment modes. Self-hosted sandboxes move the tool-execution layer (code runs, file I/O, shell commands) out of Anthropic-managed containers and into your own infrastructure or a managed provider (Cloudflare microVMs, Daytona, Modal, or Vercel). The agent orchestration loop — context management, error recovery, retries — stays on Anthropic's servers. MCP tunnels add a lightweight gateway you deploy inside your network: it opens a single outbound encrypted connection so Claude can reach private MCP servers, internal databases, and APIs without any inbound firewall rules or public DNS entries.
detail.whoItsFor: Platform engineers and AI leads at regulated enterprises (banks, insurers, healthcare) who have blocked agent pilots because tool execution was leaving their network boundary. Also relevant to any team that needs custom runtime images, large compute for long builds, or wants existing audit logs and DLP controls to apply automatically to agent runs.
pros: Files, repos, and runtime packages never leave your network perimeter
Existing audit logging and DLP tools apply automatically — no new compliance work
MCP tunnels require zero inbound firewall changes; single outbound encrypted connection only
Works with both Managed Agents and the Messages API, so it's not locked to the agentic product
cons: Agent orchestration loop still runs on Anthropic servers — fully on-prem is not possible
MCP tunnels are research preview only; requires access request, not self-serve yet
Self-hosted sandbox setup adds infra overhead; teams without Cloudflare/Daytona/Modal/Vercel need to configure their own sandbox client
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
### Prerequisites
- Anthropic API key with Claude Platform access (not Bedrock-only)
- Access to the Claude Console (console.anthropic.com)
- For MCP tunnels: request early access at console.anthropic.com → Settings → MCP Tunnels
- Supported sandbox providers: Cloudflare Workers (microVMs), Daytona, Modal, or Vercel

### 1. Install the Claude SDK (Python)

```bash
pip install anthropic>=0.52.0
```

### 2. Configure self-hosted sandbox (Daytona example)

```python
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()

agent = client.beta.managed_agents.create(
    model="claude-opus-4-7",
    sandbox={
        "type": "self_hosted",
        "provider": "daytona",
        "config": {
            "workspace_id": "my-workspace",
            "api_url": "https://my-daytona-instance.example.com",
            "api_key": "DAYTONA_API_KEY"
        }
    },
    task="Audit the /src directory for hardcoded secrets and produce a findings report"
)
print(agent.result)
```

**Gotcha:** The `sandbox.provider` field is case-sensitive and must exactly match one of: `cloudflare`, `daytona`, `modal`, `vercel`. An unrecognized value silently falls back to Anthropic-hosted execution — check `agent.sandbox_used` in the response to confirm your sandbox was actually applied.

### 3. Configure MCP tunnels (research preview)

Deploy the tunnel gateway inside your private network:

```bash
# Download the Anthropic MCP tunnel gateway binary
curl -L https://releases.anthropic.com/mcp-tunnel/latest/linux-amd64 -o mcp-tunnel
chmod +x mcp-tunnel

# Start the tunnel, pointing at your internal MCP server
./mcp-tunnel \
  --workspace-id YOUR_WORKSPACE_ID \
  --token YOUR_MCP_TUNNEL_TOKEN \
  --target http://internal-mcp-server:8080
```

Then register the tunnel in the Claude Console:
- Navigate to **Settings → MCP Tunnels → Add Tunnel**
- Paste the tunnel ID printed by the binary above

The tunnel token and workspace ID are obtained from console.anthropic.com after early-access approval.

### 4. Verify the configuration

```python
agent = client.beta.managed_agents.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
    tools=[{"type": "mcp", "tunnel_id": "YOUR_TUNNEL_ID"}],
    task="List all tables in the internal Postgres database"
)
print(agent.result)
```

learn.name: OpenAI Codex (Goal Mode GA + CLI)
learn.oneLineDescription: Define an outcome + success criteria; Codex runs autonomously until the goal is met.

detail.whatItDoes: OpenAI's Codex is an agentic coding product available as a desktop app, IDE extension, and CLI. This week, Goal Mode graduated to general availability: you define an outcome (e.g. 'all tests passing on the feature/auth branch') and success criteria, and Codex loops autonomously — writing code, running tests, reading diffs — until those criteria are met or it gives up and reports back. The CLI (`codex`) also received richer TUI controls, improved `@mentions` search for pulling in file context, expanded remote workflows, a refreshed Python SDK, and `codex doctor` diagnostics for debugging connectivity and auth. Appshots (macOS only) let you attach a live app window to a Codex thread with a hotkey, so the agent can see the actual UI state.
detail.whoItsFor: Engineers who want a Claude Code-style agentic loop without switching away from the OpenAI ecosystem. Teams running ChatGPT Business who want to ship longer coding tasks without approving every step. Particularly useful for CI-adjacent work: fix a failing test suite, migrate a dependency, or run a lint pass across a large repo.
pros: Goal Mode GA: set outcome + success criteria and walk away — no step-by-step approvals required
Available across app, IDE extension, and CLI — consistent experience on all surfaces
Appshots give the agent live visual context from a running app window (macOS)
codex doctor diagnoses auth and sandbox issues before they waste agent time
cons: Windows sandbox support still in preview — full Goal Mode on Windows is not yet stable
Goal Mode can run indefinitely on underspecified criteria; bad success criteria = wasted tokens
Shared plugins (workspace plugin reuse) require ChatGPT Business plan — not available on Plus/Pro
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
### Prerequisites
- macOS 13+ or Linux (Windows in preview)
- Node 20+ for the CLI
- OpenAI API key or ChatGPT Pro/Business subscription

### 1. Install the Codex CLI

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex
codex --version
# Should print 1.x.x
```

### 2. Authenticate

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
# Or use the interactive login:
codex auth login
```

### 3. Run a basic task

```bash
cd /path/to/your/repo
codex run "Add JSDoc comments to all exported functions in src/"
```

### 4. Use Goal Mode (the new GA feature)

```bash
codex goal \
  --outcome "All Jest tests pass on the feature/auth branch" \
  --success-criteria "npm test exits 0 with no skipped tests" \
  --branch feature/auth \
  --max-iterations 40
```

Codex will loop: write → test → inspect output → fix → repeat, up to `--max-iterations` times.

**Gotcha:** `--success-criteria` is evaluated by the model, not by a shell exit code. Write it as an unambiguous, observable statement. Vague criteria like 'code looks good' cause the agent to self-terminate early. Use exit codes or grep patterns where possible:

```bash
codex goal \
  --outcome "Migrate lodash imports to native ES2026 equivalents" \
  --success-criteria "grep -r 'lodash' src/ returns no matches AND npm test exits 0"
```

### 5. Diagnose issues

```bash
codex doctor
# Checks: API key validity, sandbox connectivity, Node version, disk space
```

learn.name: ml-intern (Hugging Face agentic ML engineer)
learn.oneLineDescription: Autonomous agent that reads papers, fine-tunes models, and uploads artifacts to Hugging Face Hub.

detail.whatItDoes: ml-intern is an open-source autonomous agent built by Hugging Face that handles the repetitive back-half of ML work: reading papers, finding relevant datasets on HF Hub, fine-tuning models in a sandboxed environment, uploading training traces to a private HF dataset, and returning finished weights. It runs an agentic loop up to 300 iterations with built-in approval gates for sensitive operations (model pushes, dataset writes). Two usage modes: interactive chat for exploration, or single-prompt headless execution ('go fine-tune this model on this dataset and push the weights'). Every session trace uploads to a private HF dataset, making every run a debuggable, shareable artifact rather than a vanished terminal session.
detail.whoItsFor: ML engineers and researchers who spend significant time on fine-tuning grunt work — monitoring training jobs, iterating on hyperparameters, pulling datasets. Particularly useful for teams already on Hugging Face Hub who want to automate model iteration without building their own agentic scaffolding. Also useful for solo builders who want to run overnight fine-tuning without babysitting.
pros: Session traces auto-upload to private HF datasets — every run is reproducible and shareable
Built-in approval gates prevent destructive pushes without confirmation
Headless mode enables fire-and-forget fine-tuning jobs without an open terminal
MIT license; 8,100+ GitHub stars in first weeks
cons: Requires a Hugging Face account with write access to Hub — not usable without HF credentials
300-iteration cap means very long fine-tuning runs may need manual continuation
No built-in cost controls for GPU compute; expensive jobs on HF Spaces can surprise you
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
### Prerequisites
- Python 3.11+
- Hugging Face account with a write-access token (`hf_...`)
- At least 16GB RAM for local fine-tuning; GPU optional but recommended

### 1. Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/huggingface/ml-intern
cd ml-intern
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

### 2. Set credentials

```bash
export HF_TOKEN="hf_your_token_here"
# Optionally set a backing LLM for the agent brain:
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."   # uses Claude Sonnet 4.6 by default
# or
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
```

### 3. Interactive mode

```bash
ml-intern chat
# > Fine-tune distilbert-base-uncased on the ag_news dataset for text classification
# Agent will: search HF Hub, pull dataset, configure trainer, run fine-tune, push weights
```

### 4. Headless / single-prompt mode

```bash
ml-intern run \
  --task "Fine-tune HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M on imdb for sentiment classification. \
          Push weights to my-org/smollm2-imdb-sentiment. \
          Target val accuracy > 90%." \
  --max-iterations 150 \
  --require-approval push  # Require human confirmation before any Hub push
```

### 5. Review session traces

```bash
# Session traces are automatically pushed to HF as a private dataset:
# https://huggingface.co/datasets/YOUR_USERNAME/ml-intern-traces
ml-intern traces list
ml-intern traces show SESSION_ID
```

**Gotcha:** By default, ml-intern uses `HF Spaces` for GPU compute, which bills against your HF billing account. Set `--compute local` to run on your own machine and avoid unexpected charges:

```bash
ml-intern run --task "..." --compute local --device cuda
```

learn.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash API
learn.oneLineDescription: Google's fastest frontier model: GA today, outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding and agentic benchmarks.

detail.whatItDoes: Gemini 3.5 Flash is now generally available via the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and Antigravity. It combines frontier-level reasoning with Flash-series latency: Google claims 4x faster output tokens per second than competing frontier models. On benchmarks, it outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (76.2%), GDPval-AA (1656 Elo), and MCP Atlas (83.6%). It accepts text, image, audio, and video inputs and is natively integrated into Antigravity 2.0 for agentic coding workflows. It replaces Gemini 3.1 Flash as the recommended daily-driver for developer applications.
detail.whoItsFor: Any developer currently using Gemini 1.5 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Flash, or who wants a fast, cost-efficient model for agentic pipelines, RAG, code generation, or multimodal apps. Direct swap-in for existing Gemini API integrations — model ID update only.
pros: GA today — available in Gemini API, AI Studio, Vertex AI, and Antigravity immediately
4x faster output token speed vs. rival frontier models per Google benchmarks
Beats Gemini 3.1 Pro on agentic and coding benchmarks at Flash speed and price
Native multimodal: text, image, audio, video input
cons: Gemini 3.5 Pro (deeper reasoning variant) still in testing — not GA yet
Benchmark claims are Google self-reported; third-party validation is early
Pricing not yet confirmed for high-volume tiers; watch for rate limit changes post-launch
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
### Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+ or Node 20+
- Gemini API key from [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey)

### 1. Install the SDK

```bash
pip install google-genai
```

### 2. Basic text generation

```python
import os
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"])

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash",   # <-- new model ID
    contents="Explain the difference between MCP tunnels and a standard reverse proxy."
)
print(response.text)
```

### 3. Streaming (recommended for agentic / long outputs)

```python
for chunk in client.models.generate_content_stream(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash",
    contents="Write a FastAPI service that proxies requests to an internal MCP server."
):
    print(chunk.text, end="", flush=True)
```

### 4. Multimodal (image + text)

```python
import pathlib

image_bytes = pathlib.Path("screenshot.png").read_bytes()

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash",
    contents=[
        {"mime_type": "image/png", "data": image_bytes},
        "Describe every UI element visible in this screenshot."
    ]
)
print(response.text)
```

**Gotcha:** The model ID is `gemini-3.5-flash` — NOT `gemini-3.5-flash-001` or `gemini-3.5-flash-latest`. Passing an unrecognized variant string silently falls back to the previous default model. Check `response.model` in the response object to confirm which model actually ran.
